issues.title: Clarify strategy for `messageType`
issues.body:
In our message definitions, we use `messageType` to represent the type of message:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1108513/199194312-0c936c35-fba7-444d-b0b7-b4be7fd2a586.png)

But, when we actually send a message, the `messageType` details gets dropped, and it gets sent as `CUSTOM_MESSAGE`:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1108513/199194451-c7c2ba71-30e6-4117-a014-fe5f31e85127.png)

Note: we do also have a `messageType` in the `message.details` - but this is being used as the placeholder for the template id to be used to edit the message.  The `MessageDetails` element is common to all message types, but the template only belongs in the `CUSTOM_MESSAGE` structure. So, we should both rename `details.messageType` to `details.templateId` AND we should move the field up into `MessageCustom`

Here is what I _think_ we have to do:
- simplify `MessageCustom`, since it contains some legacy design decisions:
    - remove `gameTurn` (since its in MessageDetails)
    - remove `feedback`  (since we have custom message type for that)
    - remove `infoType` (since we handle that in `messageType`, too)
    - we should do _something_ with `isOpen` - since that doesn't belong in the database, it's just for this client
- modify `postNewMessage` and `saveMessage` to take a `messageType` field. (Hey, do we need both methods? Can we just use one?)
- modify `postNewMessage` to call `checkReference` if there is a `message.message.reference` field - regardless of the `messageType` (it looks like it is currently doing an extensive `allDocs()` server round-trip before sending every new message)
- avoid two instances of `postNewMessage`.  Do we need both? If we do, one should be renamed to better explain its use.
- modify calls to `saveMessage` to introduce `messageType`
- modify mock/sample data to use correct message type (esp. PT-9 wargame in SQLite)
